To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the choice of contract depends on the relative market power of upstream firms and (2) the choice of the mode of competition depends on the relative bargaining power of the upstream and downstream firms.

the endogenous choice between price (Bertrand or quantity (Cournot)) contract is the dominant mode of product market interaction when two part tariff pricing mechanism is determined through centralisation Nash bargaining.

The endogenous choice of the mode of contract is determined by the bargaining power between the upstream and downstream firms, and the level of social efficiency is the same regardless the mode of competition in the product market.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implications of endogenous choice of contract in the context of two part tariff.
the endogenous choice between price and quantity contract and the welfare implications of two part tariffs in a vertical structure.
the endogenous choice between price and quantity contracts and the implications of this endogenous choice in a vertical structure with two part tariff pricing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endogenously chosen contract in the downstream market does not affect social welfare.
the two part tariff is a superior contract to both price and quantity contract in the sense that it maximises social welfare.
the endogenous choice between price and quantity contract in a two part tariff pricing scheme does not affect the level of social welfaie.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the choice of price contract in the downstream market and two-part tariff pricing in the upstream market is the optimal strategy for the firms when the bargaining is done through centralised Nash bargain.
the choice of contract is not a determinant of social welfare in a vertically related structure.
the two part tariff contract is the most effective contract in a vertically related structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mode of product competition is not a determinant of the social welfare.
the choice of contract in a two part tariff structure can be endogenous and is determined by the bargaining power of the two parties in the upstream market.
the choice of product market competition mode is not a relevant consideration in the presence of two part tariff.
